predecessors.name: Karluk Yabghu
predecessors.text: the Karluk country of Zhetysu: 'the Karluk yabghu declared himself khagan as Bilge Kul Qadir Khan' when the Uyghur Khaganate fell in 840

successors.name: Eastern Kara-Khanid Khanate
successors.text: the Eastern Khanate, 'capital at Balasaghun and later Kashgar'

successors.name: Western Kara-Khanid Khanate
successors.text: the Western Khanate in Transoxiana, 'making Samarkand the capital'

ledger.x: 840: the Karluk khagan founds the Kara-Khanid Khanate.
990: Hasan Bughra Khan invades the Samanids.
999: Nasr takes Bukhara and ends the Samanids.
999: the contest ends with the Samanid fall.
1006: Yusuf Qadir Khan of Kashgar conquers Khotan.
1045: the Khanate divides into an Eastern and a Western Khanate.

wars.name: Samanid conquest of Talas
wars.outcome: Ismail Samani took Talas and Taraz from the Karluks and converted the Nestorian church into a mosque.

wars.name: Khotan-Kara-Khanid wars
wars.outcome: Khotan briefly took Kashgar in 970; in 1006 Yusuf Qadir Khan of Kashgar conquered Khotan and ended the kingdom.

wars.name: Karakhanid-Samanid wars
wars.outcome: Hasan Bughra Khan took Isfijab, Ferghana, Samarkand and Bukhara in 990-992 (Harun took Bukhara in 992 and the Samanids returned); Nasr took Chach, Samarkand and Bukhara by 999 and the Samanids ended; the Oxus became the Ghaznavid-Kara-Khanid boundary.

wars.name: Seljuk-Kara-Khanid conflict
wars.outcome: After the Seljuk victory over the Ghaznavids at Dandanaqan (1040) 'Conflict with the Karakhanids broke out, but the Karakhanids were able to withstand attacks by the Seljuks initially'; no land changed hands.

certainty.note: Frontiers between steppe, oasis and mountain are approximate; the Oxus frontier with the Ghaznavids from 999 ('The Oxus River thus became the boundary between the two rival empires') is the one firm line.
